My family has worked this land in Quzhou for generations. I have about 6 mu. At 65, my back is not what it used to be, and my son works in the city, so I manage mostly alone. I know wheat and maize. I have always planted wheat and maize. That is what I will do again.

In October I sow winter wheat on all 6 mu. I buy the improved variety seeds from the county seed station — I used Shimai 15 last year and the yield was decent. I do not trust my own saved seed anymore, the quality has declined. I will deep plough before seeding, as I always do. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate four times: before sowing, once in winter to protect roots from freezing, at jointing, and at grain filling. Two rounds of pesticide — one for aphids in spring, one fungicide at heading. I expect around 450 jin per mu. Not great, not bad.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant summer maize on the same 6 mu. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed — everyone around here uses it, the seed seller always has it, and I know what to expect. I seed directly into the stubble with the rotary machine my neighbor owns; we share it. I apply fertilizer twice — base fertilizer at seeding and topdress at the big bell stage. I only irrigate if there is drought; usually summer rain is enough for one or two extra irrigations. I spray once for stem borer and once for fall armyworm if I see it. Yield should be around 550 jin per mu.

I will not try cotton or vegetables. Too much labor, too much risk, too uncertain on price. Wheat and maize the government buys. I sleep easier.
